title: Can an expression have more letter-numbers than terms?
description: Three more claims are checked, then the terms and the letter-numbers are counted in every corrected form. The letter-numbers are never more than the terms. The video ends with the pencil sales of the shop.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number outside a bracket multiplies every term, like terms are added once, and the letter-numbers in a simplified form are never more than its terms. Watch for students who open a bracket but leave the like terms unadded.

source: Check claims 9 to 11, then compare the number of terms with
video_script.why: A learner sees that every letter-number needs a term to sit in, so the letter-numbers cannot be more than the terms.
video_script.substitution: the book's last three claims, then the count of terms and letter-numbers in all eleven corrected forms
video_script.anchor: the last three claims of the book and the list of all the corrected forms
video_script.payoff_line: Every corrected form has no more letter-numbers than terms.

final_answer.value: 30w + 15x; 3j + 6k + 9h + 12 stays; 8r + 12s + 20; the letter-numbers are never more than the terms
final_answer.spoken: thirty w plus fifteen x; the middle one stays; eight r plus twelve s plus twenty; the letter-numbers are never more than the terms

maths_rules: 3j + 6k + 9h + 12 has no bracket and no like terms, so it is already simplest; 3(j + 2k + 3h + 4) is not simpler

terms and letter-numbers: 3a + 2b has 2 and 2; 0 has 1 and 0; 6p + 12 has 2 and 1; x - y has 2 and 2; 3 + 6z has 2 and 1; x + 5 has 2 and 1; 5y - 6 has 2 and 1; 6p + 3q has 2 and 2; 30w + 15x has 2 and 2; 3j + 6k + 9h + 12 has 4 and 3; 8r + 12s + 20 has 3 and 2
in every case the number of letter-numbers is at most the number of terms
real life: pencil sales 5c + 3c + 10c = 18c is one term with one letter-number

narration: <bookmark mark='terms'/>The parts of an expression joined by plus or minus signs are called terms.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>Letters such as w and x stand for numbers, and we call them letter-numbers.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>The number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside it.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Given, the claim about five times the bracket two w plus three x plus four w. It says ten w plus fifteen x plus twenty w.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Next, three j plus six k plus nine h plus twelve. The claim takes three outside a bracket, leaving j plus two k plus three h plus four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Last, four times the bracket two r plus three s plus five. The claim says minus twenty minus eight r minus twelve s.

marks.find: the words right form and compare terms with letter-numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to correct each claim, then compare terms with letter-numbers.

marks.inside: 2w and 4w inside the bracket are circled and joined into 6w
marks.mult: 5 × 6w + 5 × 3x = 30w + 15x is written, and the claim is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='inside'/>Step one, add the like terms inside the bracket first. Two w plus four w is six w.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Five times six w is thirty w, and five times three x is fifteen x.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 3j + 6k + 9h + 12 has no bracket and no like terms, so it is already in its simplest form

narration: <bookmark mark='none'/>Step two, look at three j plus six k plus nine h plus twelve. It has no bracket and no like terms.
<bookmark mark='bracket'/>It is already in its simplest form. The claim adds a bracket, which is not simpler.

narration: <bookmark mark='arrows'/>Step three, the four multiplies every term in the bracket.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Four times two r is eight r. Four times three s is twelve s. Four times five is twenty.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, count the terms and the letter-numbers in every corrected form.
<bookmark mark='few'/>Three eigh plus two b has two terms and two letter-numbers. Six p plus twelve has two terms and one.
<bookmark mark='many'/>Three j plus six k plus nine h plus twelve has four terms and three letter-numbers. Eight r plus twelve s plus twenty has three terms and two.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>In every case, the letter-numbers are never more than the terms.
